subject: AWS Marketplace onboarding: product page requirements and copy walkthrough
messages:
From: Sarah Mitchell <sarah.mitchell@amazon.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Marketplace onboarding — product page requirements

Hi Mina,

Great to meet you on the quick intro yesterday. I pulled your draft listing and engineering assets and have a short list of missing items we need to complete the Marketplace product page and kick off co-sell enablement: 

1) Product overview (150-200 words) that emphasizes customer outcomes and supported deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private).
2) Two product screenshots (recommended 1200x600) — one for the hero and one showing the console/UX.
3) AMI/AMI-snapshot ID or container image reference (if using AMI-based offering).
4) Pricing SKU mapping and short footnote text for usage tiers (pay-as-you-go, reserved).
5) Short security attestation / data handling blurb (SOC2 scope, retention, KMS).
6) Co-sell one-liner (20-30 words) targeted to AWS seller/sdr audiences.

If you can provide these by Tuesday we can get the listing into the publisher console and start the co-sell intake. If you'd prefer, we can do a 30-minute walkthrough and I can annotate copy live — happy to coordinate. 

Thanks,
Sarah Mitchell
AWS Marketplace Partner Onboarding

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace onboarding — product page requirements

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear checklist. Sending an initial pass attached. Highlights below and a couple of open questions for the listing UX: 

- Product overview (attached in product_page_draft.md): ~180 words, emphasizes predictable latency, dedicated/private options, and cost controls (caching/batching).
- Screenshots: attached one architecture diagram and a console hero screenshot (screenshot-architecture.png).
- AMI: we are offering AMI-based private image for some customers; I noted a placeholder in the draft — engineering will provide final AMI ID by Monday.
- Pricing: attached tier mapping (pricing-tier-proposal.xlsx) — includes PAYG per-token and reserved monthly vCPU/GPU commit rows.
- Security blurb: attached security_statement_redwood.pdf — short SOC2 scope and KMS note, plus a link to our compliance page.
- Co-sell one-liner: "Redwood Inference: predictable, low-latency LLM inference with unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

Open questions for you: where do we surface the reserved capacity / burst options in the Marketplace UX — as SKUs or as a footnote? Also, AWS Marketplace tends to surface a single hero benefit line — Ben / Karthik, can you weigh in on the headline below?

Proposed hero headline (draft):
"High-performance LLM inference for production — predictable latency, lower unit cost, multi-deployment flexibility."

Attachments: product_page_draft.md (copy + short bullets), screenshot-architecture.png (hero), security_statement_redwood.pdf, pricing-tier-proposal.xlsx

Thanks — I can hop on a quick review if helpful.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace onboarding — product page requirements

Mina — nice draft. Quick inline notes: 

- Hero headline: tighten to "Production LLM inference: predictable latency, optimized cost." (shorter, AWS customers scan fast).
- Co-sell one-liner: make it action-oriented: "Enable production LLMs with predictable latency and unified deployment options."
- Pricing footnote: clarify what "reserved" means (monthly commit with rollover vs strict reservation). We should avoid "burst" language unless we map to a SKU.

I'll make the three edits in product_page_draft.md and send an updated file by EOD. We should include a 1-paragraph case blurb about a pilot with an early beta customer (no logo yet) — helps co-sell hooks. 

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace GTM, Redwood Inference

- Headline: the shorter Ben suggested is better for the hero; we'll use your 20-word one-liner for the co-sell CTA.
- Pricing SKUs: please convert the reserved capacity row into a separate SKU entry and annotate whether commit rolls over. That makes procurement and pricing page display simpler.
- Security: the attached PDF is sufficient for initial listing; we may ask for the SOC2 report during contract signature.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Upload the final product copy (hero + bullets + one-liner) into the seller portal.
2) Convert reserved pricing row into a SKU in pricing-tier-proposal.xlsx and re-upload.
3) Provide AMI ID or container reference by next Monday.

I'll start the co-sell intake once the seller portal has your final copy; I've created the publisher record and sent the DocuSign for the seller agreement: https://www.docusign.com/sign/REDWOOD-AWS-SELLER-AGREEMENT-2027 

If you prefer a 30-minute walkthrough I have a slot Tuesday 10am PT.
